entries.speaker: Eric Weinstein
entries.quote: It is a serious advantage that we can afford to look at ourselves and say, we don’t do everything perfectly, and we want to know the truth… We limit our own ability to use cowboy science to drive the rest of the world. And quite honestly, we’re giving away our biggest advantage, which is the middle finger. The American ability to say, screw you to a supervisor who tells you what is true and what isn’t true, a young person should be able to say, hey, I think my field is going in entirely the wrong direction, and I’m willing to bet my career on it. Don’t interfere.
entries.work: Eric Weinstein, in “Eric Weinstein: The State of American Science, Breakthrough Coverups, and the Danger of Physics,” All-In Podcast

entries.speaker: Eric Weinstein
entries.quote: And I will say in particular, theoretical physics, theoretical physics is the only profession to have lost free speech because of something called restricted data where I am not allowed to put pen to paper to write down a physics equation if in any way it affects nuclear weapons. Well, try doing really good physics in a way that doesn’t affect, you know, hadrons and nucleons. It’s impossible. So you have this threat, right, that somehow the law, I’m not even protected by the First Amendment.
entries.work: Eric Weinstein, in “Eric Weinstein: The State of American Science, Breakthrough Coverups, and the Danger of Physics,” All-In Podcast

entries.speaker: Eric Weinstein
entries.quote: So my claim is that if you want to think about Walter White as a paradigm, you have to go back to something called the United States versus Progressive magazine in which the Teller Ulam design for the thermonuclear weapon was put forward by a publication. And the government said, no, no, this is restricted data. We need prior injunction. This is the most dangerous piece of geometry. This is Stan Ulam’s work.
entries.work: Eric Weinstein, in “Eric Weinstein: The State of American Science, Breakthrough Coverups, and the Danger of Physics,” All-In Podcast

entries.speaker: Eric Weinstein
entries.quote: Now, that secret got published. And the only reason the government didn’t go after, Howard, what is it, Howard Morl[and], is that we stupidly declassified all sorts of pieces and shards of this. And he went to the Los Alamos Library, and he pieced it together.
entries.work: Eric Weinstein, in “Eric Weinstein: The State of American Science, Breakthrough Coverups, and the Danger of Physics,” All-In Podcast

entries.speaker: Eric Weinstein
entries.quote: What happened in 1940 is that something that you’ve never heard of called the reference committee was established inside of the National Research Council… a guy named [Breit], B-R-E-I-T, formed something called the reference committee inside the National Research Council so that if you submitted a paper on chain reaction physics to a journal, it got shunted into the National Research Council, and they would return it to you saying, unfortunately, you know, these results are really preliminary. We don’t see this as being at the level of the journal… This is how people outside of the Manhattan Project, outside of the White Badges, treated their colleagues who weren’t allowed inside the Manhattan Project.
entries.work: Eric Weinstein, in “Eric Weinstein: The State of American Science, Breakthrough Coverups, and the Danger of Physics,” All-In Podcast

entries.speaker: Eric Weinstein
entries.quote: So my claim is, if you don’t know the story of John Aristotle Phillips, the substandard physicist who in his Princeton PhD thesis is the Princeton mascot, said, look, I’m not very good, Freeman Dyson, I want to use the fact that I’m not very good to do something amazing. Tell me whether or not you will let me come up with the plan for an atomic bomb. And Freeman Dyson said, I will give you no help, but I’ll tell you whether it will work. So the substandard physicists put together this and he submitted his junior thesis. And I forget whether it’s page 24, but that thesis is not in the library and the government removed the page that has the plan.
entries.work: Eric Weinstein, in “Eric Weinstein: The State of American Science, Breakthrough Coverups, and the Danger of Physics,” All-In Podcast

entries.locus: c. 48:14; Weinstein is voicing what he calls “the cover story”
entries.quote: Let's look at the cover story. Okay. The cover story would be, you know, we are so good at trading that we don't even allow people who know markets into our firm. We only hire people in directly relevant subjects of physics, like particle theorists, like differential geometers, like machine learning experts. And we have a very strange thing that we have a very close relationship with the Brookhaven National Laboratory. And by the way, there's a middling university right next door who happens to be absolutely world class historically in the exact subjects that would be relevant to doing next level physics.
